title: Non-deterministic /api/links ORDER BY causes unstable pagination on ties
description: GET /api/links (backend/src/routes/links.rs) orders by created_at (or click_count) DESC with no secondary tiebreaker. Rows with identical timestamps (e.g. bulk-created links) have undefined relative order across separate query executions in SQLite, so offset-based pagination (LIMIT/OFFSET) can theoretically skip or duplicate a row between page 1 and page 2 fetches. This is a plausible root cause for reports of links missing from the dashboard list. Fix: add a stable secondary ORDER BY key (id) to both the count-independent ordering and confirm LIMIT/OFFSET stays consistent.
acceptance_criteria: ORDER BY has a deterministic secondary key; verified total item count across all pages always equals the reported total with no dupes/gaps in a seeded multi-page scenario.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: deterministic secondary ORDER BY key in /api/links (backend/src/routes/links.rs); /healthz now mounted at both /api/healthz and /healthz (backend/src/routes/health.rs); removed the sticky-thead rendering bug on the desktop links table that produced a phantom gap above the header (src/components/links/links-table.tsx). Backend: cargo check + full test suite (124 unit + 16 integration) pass. Frontend: tsc --noEmit + vite build pass. Design reviewed across light/dark themes and desktop/mobile breakpoints on all dashboard pages (links list, new link, bulk, analytics summary + per-link, edit link, settings) with a seeded 35-link dataset spanning 2 pages — pagination, filters, and empty/filtered-empty states all verified correct via a real seeded backend. Automated review workflow (ecc:orch-review): both backend and frontend diffs APPROVE, one LOW naming nit addressed (STICKY_TH renamed to TH_BG).

title: Dashboard links table hides the first row (sticky thead displaced by overflow-hidden)
